vulnerabilities.description: Authorization Bypass: Script directly modifies deal/listing ownership without any authorization checks or role validation. Allows unauthorized privilege escalation and data manipulation. Any user with database access could execute this script to take ownership of deals.
XSS Vulnerability: User authentication data stored in localStorage ('manus-runtime-user-info'). Makes sensitive data accessible to DOM-based XSS attacks. Should use httpOnly cookies instead.

DOM-based XSS: updateMetaTags() accepts user-controlled SEOConfig and directly sets tag content via setAttribute() without sanitization. Allows injecting malicious scripts into meta tags if config comes from untrusted input.
Plaintext Sensitive Data: Bank account numbers, routing numbers, and PayPal emails stored in plaintext in database. Should use encryption for PCI-DSS compliance and security.
Sensitive PII Storage: KYC documents and file URLs stored without apparent encryption. User financial/identity data should be encrypted at rest.
Hardcoded User Identifier: Email 'arsenijs.kardass@gmail.com' hardcoded in script. Exposes actual user data in source code. Script also lacks authorization checks.
Database Credentials Exposure Risk: DATABASE_URL contains full database credentials. If exposed in logs/errors, allows full database compromise. No credential rotation visible.
Insufficient Input Validation: generateListingStructuredData() accepts user input without validation. Dates, prices, and descriptions could be malicious if from untrusted source.
Overly Verbose Logging: console.log statements output sensitive deal/user data. Could leak PII in production logs if not properly managed.
Administrative Script in Production: Database mutation scripts checked into repo without clear access controls. Could be accidentally executed with unintended consequences.

recommendations: URGENT: Remove fix-deal-access.js or convert to proper admin endpoint with authorization checks, audit logs, and CSRF protection
Replace localStorage with httpOnly, secure, sameSite cookies for authentication data
Implement input sanitization/DOMPurify for all user-controlled content in seo.ts meta tag injection
Encrypt sensitive fields at rest: bankAccountNumber, bankRoutingNumber, paypalEmail, paymentMethods using AES-256
Encrypt KYC document URLs and stored document data; implement field-level encryption
Remove hardcoded user identifiers from scripts; use environment variables or configuration
Implement database credential rotation; use IAM authentication instead of password in DATABASE_URL where possible (AWS RDS IAM, Google Cloud SQL)
Add input validation to all schema and SEO functions; use Zod or similar validation library
Implement proper authorization middleware on all database operations and admin scripts
Set up structured logging without PII; sanitize console output in production
Add rate limiting to prevent brute force on user lookups
Implement audit logging for all sensitive operations (ownership changes, financial data access)
Use parameterized queries consistently throughout codebase (currently mixed patterns)
Move database mutation scripts outside of main codebase; require explicit approval to run
Implement CORS/CSRF protection on all admin endpoints
